Chapter 7: The Power of Empathy
It’s so tempting to look away from stories of escape and struggle, right? To think—those things only happen to other people, somewhere far away from our own lives. But if you stop and listen, every person who’s had to run or start over carries a story that, honestly, could belong to any one of us. Sometimes, the only difference is luck—where we happen to be born, or the times we’re living in.
Picture this: there’s a teacher in a new country who notices a student sitting alone at lunch. The student’s got their eyes down, barely talking. Instead of just walking by, the teacher chooses to sit down beside them, sharing a quiet meal.
Slowly, the student starts to open up—talking about home, about what they’ve lost, and what they’re hoping for. The teacher listens—not out of pity, but with real understanding. And in that simple moment, the student feels seen.
Or think about a neighbor who welcomes a family that’s just arrived by bringing over a basket of food. It might seem like a small thing, but it breaks the ice. That family, who’s probably feeling nervous and out of place, is reminded that kindness doesn’t need words—it crosses any language barrier. Little by little, trust grows, and suddenly, the whole neighborhood feels a bit warmer.
Empathy isn’t about fixing everything or making all the pain go away. It’s really about recognizing the humanity in other people—even when their experiences look nothing like our own.
Most of us don’t realize how much a simple act of understanding can mean to someone who feels invisible.
Here’s what stands out: empathy is a bridge. It lets us connect across our differences, offer real comfort, and remind each other that, no matter what, we all belong.
In a world that can feel so divided, these moments of connection? They matter more than ever.
